html:
A huge museum of ancient Egypt on the desert edge at Giza, about two kilometres from the Great Pyramid. It fully opened on 1 November 2025, after more than two decades of planning and building. It is the largest museum in the world devoted to one civilisation.

Its building, designed by an Irish firm, cuts into the slope of the plateau, with a vast glass front aimed at the pyramids. A giant granite statue of Ramesses II, moved from a busy Cairo square in 2006, stands in the entrance hall at the foot of a great staircase lined with statues.

For the first time the full treasure of Tutankhamun, some 5,000 objects found in his tomb in 1922, is shown together. The museum also holds the cedar boat buried beside the pyramid of Khufu. It takes over most of the role of the old Egyptian Museum in Tahrir Square, built in 1902.

The project went on through revolution, coups and the pandemic. Egypt hopes it will bring back tourists and help its claim that its treasures belong at home.
